ambiguities: Kind taxonomy gap: several required operations fit no kind exactly. These are in-memory composition or supply of values (envelope composition C-126, NewRackId minting C-151, transform supply C-161, passing Database/Transaction C-03), lock holding (C-01), cache invalidation and keying (C-42, C-59), and starting a transaction (C-02). They were classified by the closest kind.

ORCH/SL-5 split in library acquisition and PREPARE-W is not determined. 15.2 gives SL-5 'a fresh acquire of the library', but 19.1 step 6 and 7.1 say SL-5/the importer 'receives the opened Database', which implies another actor opens it. No actor is assigned to the pre-import re-hash, generation-id revalidation, fingerprinting, effect check or manifest keeping.

PA-6 replaces V2.1 19.1 step 2 (the size/last-write stat bracket), yet PA-6 itself, the 19.1 UNKNOWN row ('the acquisition bracket differs') and the safeguards list ('the torn-acquisition bracket (step 2)') still cite step 2. It is unclear whether the stat bracket is still required on top of authority A/B. Step 3 still records 'source stat'.

PA-6 authority A vs 19.1 step 1: step 1 opens the source with write-deny only 'when the host allows it'. No preference order or selection rule between authority A and B is given. PA-6 authority A also resembles 19.1 'Alternative A' (allowed 'only through a reviewed amendment'), and the text does not state that PA-6 is that amendment.
Section 7 says the manifest lists what PREPARE-W 'added or changed', while 7.1 says MODIFY_PREEXISTING = PROHIBITED and 'PREPARE-W only adds'. The meaning of 'changed' is undetermined.

7.1: 'PREPARE-W does not start unless the declared mode is on the allow-list', but the mode is declared in the importer's structured result, which exists only after an import. When the check happens is undetermined. The allow-list contents beyond DuplicateRecordCloning.Ignore are not given.

Outcome codes O1, O2 and O6 and the ABORT-VERIFY rule for choosing O2 vs O6 are not defined in the fragments. Section 7 gives no outcome for a copy re-hash mismatch before an import (19.1 says O2 with residue). No outcome is given for a failed generation-id revalidation or a post-run copy re-hash mismatch.

Referenced sections are absent from the input, so operations they impose cannot be compiled: 11.3 (composition rule for pre-existing definitions W-5/TBD-13, derivation of the ADD set from the closure, partial failures), 28 (fingerprint definition), 4.3/4.3.1 (CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL, SOURCE_SWAP_CONTROL, qualification), 13.1 (warm-up side DB), 14.5, 20, 25, 27.5-27.8 (EVM schema, completeness review, corpus), V3 4.2, V4 3.3/3.4, V2.2 PA-11 conditions 1-7, ADR-0036 tolerance, P-5, NG-09.
'Relevant elements' of the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD are not defined. When and by which actor the record (including homologue fingerprints) is produced is not stated; C-72 is presupposed, not stated.

Sampling points P0, PL, PS and PV are not defined in the fragments beyond their expected counts. VERIFY allows 'or the exact equivalent the Architect reviews', which leaves the verifier's transaction pattern open.

Nested transactions inside T_M: PV requires 'no nested transaction' at sampling time, and 15.3 forbids only internal Commit/Abort/Dispose/LockDocument/OpenCloseTransaction. Whether a seam may start and end a nested transaction (StartTransaction) inside T_M is not determined; such transactions would fall into the declared blind spot.

E-06 sources: 'two sources disagree (counter, own bookkeeping, events)'. Whether own bookkeeping is a mandatory second source is not stated, and events are optional ('if they exist'). The qualification controls E6-C1..C8 belong to I-07 qualification (section 4.3); when they must run relative to a CT-21D run is not stated.

IsTopTransaction is three-valued (YES/NO/UNKNOWN), but 'The log records the boolean result'. How UNKNOWN is logged is undetermined. Who owns the typed authority's implementation (shared service or per seam) is not stated.

Envelope clause (exact authored payload) applies to SL-1..SL-4, but SL-4 creates a reference. Whether SL-4 writes and reads back an envelope is not determined, and the envelope's storage object is not specified. SL-6 scans 'records', which suggests envelopes live on definitions.
The 15.3 row 'fresh reread and comparator support | 15.7' is a requirement on SL-1..SL-4, but 15.7 describes only SL-6. What SL-1..SL-4 must do to 'support' fresh reread is not determined.
'Deterministic result' is stated as a property with no prescribed verification. The mechanism, location and owner of the 'static guard' are not specified.

Naming: which actor applies the family policy is not stated. The fragments have no explicit clause requiring the seam's returned effective name to be compared with the name PREPARE-R expected. The typed failure for a sanitizer-empty name (presumably InvalidBlockName) and the actor that detects it (PREPARE-R or seam) are not stated.

Validation criteria for InvalidPlan and InvalidEnvelope are undefined. For InvalidBlockName, only the sanitizer-empty criterion is given. Which seams have a 'target space' for TargetSpaceInvalid is not stated (SL-4 at least). Which missing blocks count as 'detectable from the declared requirements' (PRE-WRITE vs POST-WRITE MissingLibraryBlocks) is not determined.

The result shape is a 'working shape'. MissingInstances and Diagnostic have no defined semantics. Whether 'handles of all created objects' covers nested entities and envelope storage objects is not stated.
SL-4 'sets layer and properties from the plan' and 'applies dynamic properties'. The properties are not enumerated.
SL-3 is 'not required' by sealed scope V1 and is referred to as 'if it is ever authorized'. Whether the orchestrator is prohibited from invoking SL-3 in V1 is not explicitly stated.
When the created-object list and PROTECTED_OBJECTS are sealed is not stated. PA-10 implies after phase A and by PV.
'Option B' (rollback compatible with Option B; EQ-4 'Option-B host evidence') is not defined in the fragments. PA-10's 'relevant containers' and 'NOD entries the kind consumes' are not enumerated.

27.2 and the V2.4 inventory gates are control-plane/validation procedures with no runtime actor; they were assigned to ORCH (control plane). 27.2's primitive categories are illustrative ('any other explicit category the inventory shows'), and the text does not map categories to seams. 27.2 lists SL-1, SL-2, SL-4 and SL-5 only, and does not say whether ORCH's own mutations (commit/abort) or SL-3 fall under the inventory. The 'bound SHA' in V2.4 is not given.
SL-1 creates 'one per depth k'. How the set of depths is derived from the plan is not stated.
